Theme

School & learning

arithmetic noun

also arithmetical, mental arithmetic, numbers

classical

Plin. NH 35.76: praecipuē arithmēticā et geōmetriā
Vitr. 1.1.4: per arithmēticēn

arithmētica, arithmēticae f.

noun, first declension

Greek ἀριθμητική, the art of numbers. Vitruvius declines it in Greek, arithmēticē, -ēs; Cicero says arithmētica, neuter plural (Att. 14.12.3).

Other words

  • numerī, numerōrum m. pl. — numbers, arithmetic

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Quint. 1.10.35: numerōrum quidem nōtitia

    Quintilian divides geometry, as mathematics was called, into numbers and figures (in numerōs atque fōrmās). Learning to count and reckon is numerāre discere (see count).

Examples

  • ubi legere et scrībere et numerāre discitur

    where one learns to read, to write and to countAug. Conf. 1.13.20

  • hominem remōtum ā dialecticīs, in arithmēticīs satis exercitātum

    a man far from logic, but well practised in arithmetic (Cicero’s host, the banker Vestorius)Cic. Att. 14.12.3

See also maths, sum, subtract, multiply, divide, times table, count.
